content: Follow this single-pass structured procedure whenever a question asks to compare numbers or counts of objects, or to subtract/filter sets. Do not apply this procedure to measurement-style questions (time, distance, continuous magnitudes). 1) Paraphrase and label: Identify the comparison operator (>, <, =, more/less, which condition) and label the two sides as Group A and Group B. If the question asks to subtract or remove, treat that as a set-difference operation on the relevant universe. 2) Decompose filters: For each group, separately list (a) attribute filters (color, size, material, finish, shape, 'tiny', 'thin', etc.) and (b) spatial/relational filters (left of, behind, in front of, near). Do not merge different kinds of filters—apply them conjunctively to define the group. 3) Apply set logic once: Compute the set for each group using explicit set operations: intersection for combined filters, difference for 'subtract' statements, union if the question explicitly aggregates multiple sets. If an object satisfies multiple subfilters, count it only once in the final set. 4) Resolve overlaps deterministically: If the same object would belong to both Group A and Group B and the question asks for exclusive membership, clarify by applying the stated operations in order (e.g., apply removals before counting). Avoid assumptions; follow the explicit textual operators in the question. 5) Out-of-scope detection: If answering requires measuring time/distance/continuous magnitude or experimental numeric measurement (measurement_target), stop and return a short, explicit refusal such as: "out_of_scope_measurement" rather than guessing. 6) Single-pass verification: Re-count each final set once more to check for missed overlaps or misapplied differences. Do not iterate multiple speculative visual crops—perform one careful deterministic pass. 7) Final output format: Return only the required answer type (integer count, Yes/No, A/B). Immediately after, on a single short line, give the minimal verification: "Group A = n; Group B = m; reasoning: [brief set operation summary]". Keep internal deliberation private and concise.
